Cautious and policy-supportive tone persists. The FOMC stresses ongoing pandemic-related risks and maintains a highly accommodative stance (near-zero rates, sustained Treasury and MBS purchases, money-market operations). The FSR adds elevated financial vulnerabilities (elevated asset valuations, high corporate leverage, funding-market fragilities), partly mitigated by effective Fed facilities and strong bank capital/liquidity.

SLOOS tilts the balance a bit more negative for growth-sensitive credit: banks report tightened standards for C&I lending and cite concerns about the economic outlook, industry-specific problems, risk tolerance, and liquidity—signals that credit supply to businesses remains constrained. Offsetting positives include easing by large banks in several mortgage categories, some strengthening in C&I demand at foreign banks, and small banks expecting stronger consumer loan demand with some easing tied to improving credit quality. Netting these, business credit headwinds outweigh housing/consumer pockets of improvement, nudging the overall tone slightly more negative than the FSR-only read.
